title: Many millions
hookLine: kaee kott: many millions worship, many millions wander, many millions are learned

cards: In India, big numbers have their own names. A lakh is a hundred thousand. A crore is ten million.
Headlines say a film earned a hundred crore; a festival drew two crore pilgrims. In Punjabi and in the old language of the Guru Granth Sahib, the word is kot, or kott.
And ashtpadi ten picks up that enormous number and swings it like a drumstick. Kaee kot. Many crores.
Many tens of millions. Line after line, in a rhythm you can feel even if you don't understand a single word.

teach.h: KAEE KOT: MANY TENS OF MILLIONS.
teach.b: The first stanza runs like this.
Kaee kot hoe poojaaree: many millions are worshippers. Many millions keep religious rites and customs. Many millions live at places of pilgrimage.
Many millions wander the forests as renunciates. Many millions listen to the Vedas. Many millions become great ascetics.
Many millions fix their minds in meditation. Many millions are poets, pondering poetry. Many millions meditate on the ever-new Name.
And the last line: Nanak, none of them can find the Creator's limit.
Look who's in the list: every kind of seeker of Guru Arjan's world, and not one is mocked or ranked. They're simply counted, with wonder, as part of the creation. Then the turn.
All those millions, every path of seeking, and none reaches the end of the One who made them. That's not a put-down of the seekers. It's a statement about how big the Creator is.
If tens of millions of sincere seekers can't measure it, nobody is going to measure it alone. Japji, which we read last year, says it too: no one can reach the end of God's praise.
Kaee kot is that same humility, set to a drumbeat.
Millions upon millions, every one of them held. Millions, all His.

how: Sikhs reading Sukhmani Sahib recite the 'kaee kot' stanzas of the tenth ashtpadi in a strong, repeated rhythm, as a hymn of wonder at the size of the creation.

o: one lakh, a hundred thousand people
seekers ranked from best to worst
tens of millions, counted with wonder

s: the 'kaee kot' stanza ranks the seekers it lists
worshippers, pilgrims, ascetics, poets: counted with wonder, not ranked.
a kot, or crore, is ten million
a lakh is a hundred thousand; a crore is ten million.
the stanza ends saying none of them can find the Creator's limit
a statement of how big the Creator is.

games.q: tens of millions of sincere seekers, every style. by the stanza, what's true of all of them?
o: only one group gets it right.
none of them can find the Creator's limit.
games.why: Nanak, none of them can find the Creator's limit: humility, set to a drumbeat.

practice: Picture one person who prays differently from you, or doesn't pray at all, and wish them well: may they be safe, may they be at peace.

Then widen the wish to a town, a country, the whole planet, eight billion, more than eight hundred crore; you can't picture every face, and that's the point. If you pray, you can hold them all before God.

wordCard.voice: Many millions. Kaee kot: tens of millions of seekers of every kind, counted with wonder, and none finding the Creator's limit.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: kot, ten million, a crore; 'kaee kot', many tens of millions, is ashtpadi ten's refrain.

carryVoice: Your line: millions, all his. Every path, every seeker, held. That's day four hundred seventy-five.

sources.work: Guru Granth Sahib (Guru Arjan, Gauri Sukhmani)

sources.ref: Japji Sahib, pauri 24 (Ang 5): no end to His praises
